body:
Extend the per-request early-exit pattern from #31981 to the remaining kernels whose grid or inner loop spans the full captured width: DSA decode / target-verify metadata, FA3 decode metadata, TRTLLM MHA graph metadata, extend attention (regular and unified), the DSA indexer K+S gather, and the sparse prefill index transform.

<details>
<summary>Appendix: microbenchmark results (kernel x setting, main vs this PR, n=10)</summary>

Methodology: 10 interleaved A/B process pairs (main / PR alternating); each sample is one Triton `do_bench` (100ms warmup + 1000ms measurement); values are mean +- std over the 10 runs; verdicts use a paired t-test (n=10, two-sided 5%). `SKIP` = most blocks are past the per-request live length, the early exit fires; `NOSKIP` = every block is live, the exit never fires (worst case, pure guard overhead). "n.s." = not statistically significant.

### Metadata kernels (decode / verify graph replay)

| Kernel | Setting | main (us) | PR (us) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fused_dsa_decode_metadata` | SKIP bs=1, width=16384, seq=1024 | 5.87 +- 0.11 | 5.73 +- 0.09 | -2.4% |
| | SKIP bs=8 | 6.29 +- 0.11 | 6.04 +- 0.18 | -3.9% |
| | SKIP bs=64 | 10.71 +- 0.17 | 10.10 +- 0.15 | -5.6% |
| | half live: bs=8, seq=8192 | 6.28 +- 0.17 | 6.26 +- 0.21 | n.s. |
| | SKIP bs=8, width=65536, no wide table | 8.12 +- 0.17 | 7.66 +- 0.15 | -5.7% |
| | NOSKIP bs=8 | 6.27 +- 0.14 | 6.39 +- 0.15 | +2.0% n.s. (p~0.06) |
| | NOSKIP bs=64 | 10.69 +- 0.19 | 10.73 +- 0.07 | n.s. |
| `fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata` | SKIP bs=1 / 8 / 32, seq=1024 | 6.00 / 8.07 / 15.55 | 5.81 / 7.63 / 15.02 | -3.0% / -5.5% / -3.4% |
| | NOSKIP bs=8 / bs=32 | 8.04 / 15.50 | 8.04 / 15.54 | flat / n.s. |
| `normal_decode_set_metadata` (FA3) | SKIP bs=1, page=1 | 5.88 +- 0.17 | 5.84 +- 0.08 | n.s. |
| | SKIP bs=8, page=1 | 6.35 +- 0.14 | 6.22 +- 0.14 | -2.1% |
| | SKIP bs=64, page=1 | 11.95 +- 0.18 | 7.89 +- 0.18 | **-34.0%** |
| | NOSKIP bs=8, page=1 | 6.34 +- 0.18 | 6.44 +- 0.22 | +1.7% n.s. |
| | NOSKIP bs=64, page=1 | 11.94 +- 0.14 | 9.82 +- 0.16 | -17.7% |
| | SKIP bs=8 / bs=64, page=64 | 6.70 / 12.96 | 6.22 / 9.04 | -7.1% / **-30.3%** |
| | NOSKIP bs=64, page=64 | 12.92 +- 0.14 | 10.97 +- 0.11 | -15.1% |
| `update_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata` | SKIP bs=1 / 8 / 64, seq=1024 | 11.46 / 12.15 / 16.88 | 5.60 / 5.77 / 6.08 | **-51% / -53% / -64%** |
| | NOSKIP bs=8 / bs=64 | 12.18 / 16.88 | 12.00 / 16.78 | -1.4% / n.s. |

### Attention / gather kernels

| Kernel | Setting | main (us) | PR (us) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `extend_attention_fwd` | SKIP ragged extend 7x16 + 1x4096, prefix=1024 | 4207.6 +- 4.6 | 1272.9 +- 5.5 | **3.3x** |
| | SKIP same, prefix=8192 | 30262.8 +- 42.6 | 5154.2 +- 12.3 | **5.9x** |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend 8x64 | 139.44 +- 0.11 | 138.26 +- 0.13 | -0.85% |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend 4x4096 | 4709.2 +- 8.4 | 4727.9 +- 11.4 | +0.40% |
| `extend_attention_fwd_unified` | SKIP ragged extend 7x16 + 1x4096, prefix=1024 | 5681.5 +- 15.1 | 2262.9 +- 7.1 | **2.5x** |
| | SKIP same, prefix=8192 | 35138.8 +- 105.4 | 7133.4 +- 20.1 | **4.9x** |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend 8x64 | 153.32 +- 0.33 | 153.67 +- 0.18 | +0.23% |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend 4x4096 | 9615.1 +- 26.3 | 9627.0 +- 10.8 | n.s. |
| `_get_k_and_s_triton` | NOSKIP uniform seq=1024 / 8192; SKIP ragged | 7.38 / 10.28 / 7.90 | 7.46 / 10.34 / 7.91 | n.s. (all) |
| `transform_index_page_table_prefill` | SKIP ragged extend 7x16 + 1x4096 | 128.30 +- 0.42 | 73.09 +- 0.35 | **-43.0%** |
| | NOSKIP uniform extend=64 / 512 | 40.20 / 77.62 | 40.16 / 77.62 | flat |

Notes:
- Every SKIP-scenario gain above is statistically significant (paired t-test, p < 0.05; the PR side is faster in at least 7 of 10 paired runs, usually 10 of 10).
- No metadata-kernel NOSKIP config shows a significant regression. The closest is DSA decode NOSKIP bs=8 at +2.0% (p ~ 0.06, ~+0.12us); this worst case requires seq == the captured max-context width, which real serving essentially never reaches. On the live path the `kv_len` load is issued alongside the existing `req_idx` load, so no serialized latency is added.
- For the attention kernels the guard shifts NOSKIP shapes within +-0.9% with no consistent sign (-0.85% / +0.40% / +0.23% / n.s.), i.e. code-layout jitter from the added branch rather than a systematic cost; the ragged-batch upside is 2.5-5.9x.

### Where the gains are large in practice

- `update_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata` (**2.1-2.8x**): the page-table width is the static max-context bound while real seq lens are far smaller, so the skip applies on essentially every replay; the kernel runs ~4 times per decode step per TP rank and feeds the first all-reduce, making this a per-step latency win.
- `normal_decode_set_metadata` (**-30~-34% at bs=64**): FA3 decode replay also always passes the max-context width; gains grow with batch size.
- `extend_attention_fwd` / `_unified` (**2.5-5.9x** on ragged batches): mixed-length extend batches (continuous batching, mixed chunked prefill) skip whole attention compute blocks, not just metadata copies; uniform batches (e.g. spec verify) are unchanged.
- `transform_index_page_table_prefill` (**-43%** on ragged batches): sparse prefill index transform for mixed-length batches.
- DSA decode / target-verify metadata gains are real but small (launch-bound, -2~-6% per step), consistent with the draft-extend kernel from #31981.

</details>
